acceptance.given: The package validator is invoked on input that produces diagnostic findings, including synthetic secret-like content, an absolute host path, and arbitrary source text.

oracle.expected: Every diagnostic is structured and contains none of the synthetic secret value, absolute host path, or arbitrary source text; the result preserves rule, path, and code fields and has authorizes=[].
forbidden: A diagnostic exposes a secret value.
A diagnostic exposes an absolute host path.
A diagnostic echoes arbitrary source text.
oracle.observable: Inspect every diagnostic field in the validate_package result and serialized CLI JSON after the real validator test executes.

acceptance.then: Diagnostics report structured findings without any of the three prohibited content classes.
acceptance.when: The diagnostic-sanitization test executes the real validator entry or CLI and evaluates the returned structured diagnostics.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the diagnostic-sanitization pytest selector against the real validator entry and fail when any diagnostic exposes a secret value, absolute host path, or arbitrary source text.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Sanitize validator diagnostics so structured findings never disclose secret values, absolute host paths, or arbitrary inspected source text while retaining rule IDs, relative paths, codes, and relevant boundary effects.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted state migration is required; preserve the versioned result shape and authorizes=[] when reverting implementation changes.

slice_hint.state_transition: Potentially disclosive diagnostics become structured, sanitized diagnostics emitted by validate_package and its CLI.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted core pytest command passes and proves that every diagnostic omits the synthetic secret, absolute host path, and arbitrary source text while preserving structured result fields.
